ca_jailhouse_rock_2.blurb: Jailhouse Rock is a jumbled little formation in the westernmost corner of Joshua Tree's Indian Cove, only a short stroll from where the campground road ends. All eleven routes are traditional leads. Most sit at the gentle end of the scale, from near scrambles through easy fifth class up to moderate 5.7 and 5.8 lines, with a single route reaching the 5.10 range. That makes it a friendly place for newer trad leaders or a relaxed lap with a small rack. The cliff catches sun for most of the day, so it feels sunbaked and quiet in warm weather. Grains can crumble in places, so back up your placements, and carry plenty of water since little is available nearby.

ca_farmhill_boulder.blurb: Farmhill Boulder is a small local boulder in Redwood City on the San Francisco Peninsula, about half a mile up Farmhill Boulevard from the Stulsaft Park entrance. The stone is highly featured and has a pleasant texture under the fingers. Eleven problems are spread from the very easiest grades up to V6, with a cluster of moderate lines in the V1 to V5 range and a couple of harder ones near the top. Because it is a single boulder standing close to the road, there is almost no walk-in, which makes it a quick after-work session or a stop for visiting climbers. Bring a pad and expect a short outing rather than a full day.

ca_oasis_the_2.blurb: The Oasis is a small section of the Emeralds, the I-80 corridor crag area near Emigrant Gap and the Yuba River. It holds eleven routes, a mix of five bolted lines and six traditional ones. Grades run from easy 5.5 climbing through the 5.8 to 5.10 range, which is where most of the routes sit, with a couple of hard lines in the 5.12 and 5.13 range. The routes are short and only minutes from the parking area, so it works well as a quick add-on to a day at the neighbouring walls. The wider Emeralds area is best in spring and fall, and many of its walls face northwest, offering some morning shade in summer.

ca_franklin_s_tower.blurb: Franklin's Tower is a compact riverside crag in the Upper Gorge of the Owens River Gorge, in the Eastern Sierra near Bishop. A small detached tower sits on the left and a larger formation to the right, with the river running right beside the base. Nine of the eleven routes are single-pitch sport climbs, plus a couple of trad lines, and the grades lean hard: a few climbs in the 5.8 to 5.11 range, then a bunch of quality 5.12 and 5.13 routes. It tends to feel less busy than the bigger Gorge walls. The path in squeezes between the water and the rock, so watch your footing near the river, and bring a standard sport rack with quickdraws.

ca_dave_moore_nature_area.blurb: Dave Moore Nature Area is a small day-use property along Highway 49 near Coloma, in the Sierra foothills beside the South Fork of the American River. A loop trail leads through oak woodland and pine to a scatter of granite boulders. Bouldering here is modest, with eleven problems: mostly moderate lines from V0 up to around V5, plus a couple of much harder ones. The walk is flat and takes roughly ten minutes, so it makes a good quick session if you want something other than the busier Auburn boulders. It is best thought of as a winter option when higher terrain is out of condition. There is no drinking water, so bring your own.

ca_center_wall_2.blurb: Center Wall is one of the main sport walls at Big Chief, on a ridge above Highway 89 in the Truckee River Canyon near Lake Tahoe. It holds a number of the area's most popular routes, so expect company and little solitude. All eleven routes are bolted, with a mid-grade lean: a handful of 5.8 to 5.9 warmups, a couple of 5.10s, one 5.11, and five climbs around 5.12. The climbing is steep and positive, and the canyon views are a draw. From the notch above the wall, head left a few minutes, passing Three Towers Wall and Center Cave; the wall comes just beyond. The area runs warm, so early or late sessions are more comfortable in summer.

ca_dinosaur_crag.blurb: Dinosaur Crag is a glacier-polished orange cliff band in two tiers, at roughly 9,800 feet above Ellery Lake in the Lee Vining Canyon and Tioga Road corridor. Because it sits above timberline, it can be cold and windy when the weather turns, though it catches sun in the afternoon. Of the eleven routes, nine are trad leads and two are top-rope, with crack, slab and friction climbing. Grades start around 5.5, bunch in the 5.7 and 5.11 ranges, and top out with a single line in the low 5.12 range, so it suits confident leaders more than beginners. The walk-in is short but over uneven ground, so wear sturdy shoes and plan for thin alpine air.
